metadata.note: Lancaster and Chester Railway (SC), Chester - Lancaster, 28.9 mi, and its predecessor the Cheraw and Chester Railroad (inc. 1873, 3 ft gauge; never reached Cheraw). Rule 4 splits drawn, sharing geometry: Cheraw and Chester (own operation, Chester - Fort Lawn only, before the 1883 Catawba bridge) | Charlotte, Columbia and Augusta (lessee, 1883-85) | Richmond and Danville (lessee via the CC&A, from 1 May 1886) | Cheraw and Chester in receivership (1893-96) | Lancaster and Chester (from 20 Jun 1896). NOT splits: Springs family control (Leroy 1896, Elliott 1931, Close 1959), USRA control in WWI, the Southern's 1902 gauge-conversion loan. The L&C feature has no 1917 segment: the July 1916 flood cut the line until Dec 1918.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt): L&C entry, 'Double daily, except Sunday, service is operated for freight and express only'

The road is tagged by its present name, not by old_railway_operator (a probe for old_railway_operator~'Lancaster|Cheraw|L&C|LC' returned 0 ways): the main line carries operator='Lancaster & Chester RR' / name 'Lancaster & Chester RR' / reporting_marks=LC, so a scratch Operator subclass also read operator= and name=, and excluded every way named '(SB Line)' - the ex-Southern Lancaster - Kershaw track the L&C leased in 2001, which is not this road's passenger history. fetch_gap over the Catawba crossing (34.68,-80.92 - 34.73,-80.84; the mirror returned a false empty, so the abandoned/disused ways there were re-fetched with a direct query and cached in its place) and over Chester found only industrial spurs and the SAL Great Falls Branch, and OpenHistoricalMap has no railway in the corridor. metadata.colour_choice: Richmond and Danville uses #5D4A7A, pulled programmatically from rd-chester-lenoir-chester-newton in carolina_and_northwestern_railway.geojson. No feature in data/ carried the Cheraw and Chester, the Charlotte, Columbia and Augusta or the Lancaster and Chester, so each got a new colour (#6E5A2A, #3D6E8C, #A23B2A), checked programmatically against every colour already in data/.
tracer_decisions: Drawn exactly the report's drawable spans: [1] 1879 ANCHOR, [2] 1883-1885, [3] 1886-1892, [4] 1895 ANCHOR, [5] 1898-1916, [6] 1918-1919 OPEN.
1896 not added to the 1895 anchor: the only 1896 evidence is the SC Railroad Commission fare order, a regulatory list.

The CC&A era is drawn here as its own colour, whereas carolina_and_northwestern_railway.geojson leaves the same lease undrawn on the Chester and Lenoir because its start date was unsourced there; this report has dated 1883 evidence (Fowler's 1883 Guide listing, the Oct 1883 Railroad Commission item) for this line.
Pre-1916 eras are drawn over the present Catawba bridge (see geometry_quality).
not_yet_sourced: PASSENGER END: Lancaster and Chester passenger service is confirmed to May 1919 and was gone by Dec 1951 (Official Guide Feb 1952: 'freight and express only'; index daggers at Grace, Richburg, Lancaster). The end year inside that bracket is unknown; the L&C feature's 1918-1919 segment is [OPEN]. Best next sources: Lancaster News / Chester Reporter 1920s-40s, SC Railroad Commission annual reports, 1920s-30s Official or Russell's Guides.

SOURCE CONFLICT: secondary sources (the historical marker '1896-1913', wvncrails, Wikipedia-family pages, the railroad's own history) say scheduled passenger service ended with the 1913 Hooper's Creek wreck. Lancaster News reports of a passenger coach and new schedule in Dec 1914, a through passenger-and-freight train on 23 Dec 1918 and double-daily service from 22 May 1919 contradict that; the map follows the contemporary reports. The '1913' claim may mean the end of all-passenger equipment (mixed trains thereafter) - unproven.
Hooper's Creek wreck date: 30 Jul 1913 (Yorkville Enquirer 1 Aug 1913, 'last Wednesday', 3 dead at press time) vs 30 Jun 1913 (wvncrails, train #16, 79 passengers, 5 dead).
Cheraw and Chester own operation: the CC&A lease start (between Apr 1880 and Oct 1883) is not found, and no 1880-82 passenger item was read, so only 1879 is drawn.
Richmond and Danville lease end: not found; whether the R&D 'threw up' the lease after Chester county's 1886 bond suit is not established. Drawn to 1892.
1893-94 and 1896-97: no passenger item read; very probably ran, not drawn.
Jul 1916 - Dec 1918 flood gap: Wikipedia mentions a ferry until the new bridge; whether trains ran Chester - Fort Lawn in the gap is not established. Not drawn.
Gauge conversion 1902 (ICC, Wikipedia, wvncrails) vs 1906 (Trains magazine per search summary); ICC preferred.
Whether the present Catawba bridge is the 1918 bridge, and whether the 1883-1916 bridges stood on the same line.
Headways and avg_speed_kmh are estimates throughout.
omitted: Modern excursion trains (Santa trains, Fort Lawn Spring Festival train, dinner trains, c.2006-2014): drawable NONE in the report - the years are supported but which track each excursion used is not; some ran on the 2001-leased ex-Southern Lancaster - Kershaw line.
'Springmaid Special' / 'Gay Nineties' train, 1950s-60s (Winthrop University collection): drawable NONE - no confirmed run.
Years not evidenced: 1880-1882, 1893-1894, 1896-1897, 1917, and everything after 1919.
freight_only_excluded: Everything after the unknown passenger end (before Dec 1951) to the present: freight and express only.
Great Falls Branch (abandoned 1980): no passenger evidence found.
Catawba Jct - Kershaw, 30.8 mi ex-Southern/NS, leased 2001 (OSM '(SB Line)'): freight under the L&C apart from possible excursions.
East Chester interchange with SCL (1981): freight.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN start] 1879 is the one year with passenger evidence in hand: the Yorkville Enquirer of 11 Sep 1879 reports the Chester Light Dragoons 'will have an excursion from Yorkville to Fort Lawn, on the Cheraw and Chester Railroad', and that of 25 Sep 1879 that Chester clerks 'took a pleasure trip to Fort Lawn, on the Cheraw and Chester Railroad'. Service certainly ran wider both ways - the road was built 'from about 1873 to 1879' (ICC; a construction period, not an opening date) and Fort Lawn stayed the working terminus until the Catawba bridge of 1883 - but no other year of the company's own operation is confirmed, and the date the Charlotte, Columbia & Augusta lease ended it is unknown. Do not widen without evidence. 3 ft gauge, steam (wood-burning); no animal traction found (Rule 5). Headway is an estimate (one round trip a day assumed), not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Yorkville Enquirer 11 Sep 1879 p3 and 25 Sep 1879 p3 for 1879 passenger movements to Fort Lawn; ICC valuation for the construction period (as quoted in research/branches/lancaster_and_chester_railway.txt, researched 2026-11-05; the tracer did not re-open these pages). Headway NOT sourced.

segments.note: The Charlotte, Columbia & Augusta, as lessee of the Cheraw and Chester, ran the line through to Lancaster once the Catawba bridge opened. Start 1883: the bridge was 'under way ... thought the bridge will be completed by the first day of May' (Yorkville Enquirer 29 Mar 1883), and Fowler lists the east-bank stations Catawba River (South) and Miller's Crossing from the 1883 Official Guide (Grace/Washaw from 1884); the opening month is not found. The CC&A is confirmed as operator by 2 Oct 1883 (SC Railroad Commission, Yorkville Enquirer 11 Oct 1883), but the 29 Mar 1883 item still speaks of 'the Cheraw and Chester train', so whether the CC&A or the C&C itself ran the first months of 1883 is not established. End 1885: the Richmond & Danville's lease of the CC&A 'and the Cheraw and Chester Railroad' is 'dated May 1st, 1886' (L. M. Grist letter, Yorkville Enquirer 17 Aug 1887), so the CC&A era runs to 30 Apr 1886; 1886 is drawn wholly in R&D colour. The CC&A was itself controlled by the R&D syndicate. 3 ft gauge, steam. Headway is an estimate (one round trip a day assumed), not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: Yorkville Enquirer 29 Mar 1883 p2, 11 Oct 1883 p2, 1 Apr 1886 p3 and 17 Aug 1887 p2, and Fowler's SC list (line 77, 1883G / 1884G letters) (as quoted in research/branches/lancaster_and_chester_railway.txt, researched 2026-11-05; the tracer did not re-open these pages). The CC&A lease START date is NOT sourced. Headway NOT sourced.

segments.note: The Richmond & Danville operated the Cheraw and Chester through its lease of the Charlotte, Columbia & Augusta, from 1 May 1886 (lease date per the L. M. Grist letter, Yorkville Enquirer 17 Aug 1887). In Oct 1886 'the Richmond and Danville Company will throw up its lease of the Cheraw and Chester road' if Chester county won its bond suit (Fairfield News and Herald 27 Oct 1886); whether it did so is not established. End trimmed to 1892: the R&D system entered receivership in 1892 and the C&C itself on 1 Jul 1893 (ICC), and the lease's actual end cannot be dated inside 1892-93. No dated primary passenger item from 1886-1892 was read: passenger service in this era rests on the secondary statement that the R&D ran through trains 'Lancaster SC - Lenoir with the Chester & Cheraw' (tarheelpress, via the Carolina and Northwestern report) and continuity with the 1883-85 and 1895 eras. 3 ft gauge, steam. Headway is an estimate (one round trip a day assumed), not sourced.
sources: Segment-level: lease start from Yorkville Enquirer 17 Aug 1887 p2; Fairfield News and Herald 27 Oct 1886 p4; Yorkville Enquirer 7 Jun 1893 p2 (reorganisation plan naming the C&C) (as quoted in research/branches/lancaster_and_chester_railway.txt, researched 2026-11-05; the tracer did not re-open these pages). Passenger service itself rests on tarheelpress via research/branches/carolina_and_northwestern_railway.txt, not re-checked. Lease END NOT sourced. Headway NOT sourced.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] The Cheraw and Chester in its own name, in receivership (receivers from 1 Jul 1893; foreclosure 1 Jun 1896; the Lancaster and Chester took the property by deed 20 Jun 1896 - ICC). 1895 is the one confirmed year: the Yorkville Enquirer of 27 Sep 1895 reports a marriage that 'took place on the Cheraw and Chester railroad train ... while the train waited at Knox Station', the groom being 'route agent on the Narrow Gauge railroad'. Service certainly ran wider both ways (1893-94 and early 1896), but no other year is confirmed: the April 1896 SC Railroad Commission fare order (Watchman and Southron 8 Apr 1896) lists passenger fares for the road but is a regulatory list, so 1896 is not drawn. Do not widen without evidence. 3 ft gauge, steam. Headway is an estimate (one round trip a day assumed), not sourced.

Headway NOT sourced.

segments.note: [OPEN start] Lancaster and Chester Railway (Leroy Springs), successor by foreclosure to the Cheraw and Chester from 20 Jun 1896. 1898 is the first confirmed passenger year: Lancaster Ledger 24 Aug 1898 prints 'Schedule in effect Daily except Sunday on and after May 11, 1898', Nos. 14/16 and 15/17 (two round trips) plus a Sunday-only No. 19, Lancaster - Fort Lawn - Bascombville - Richburg - Chester. 1896-97 very probably ran too but no passenger item was read, so they are not drawn. Further confirmations: a body brought 'on the L. C. train' (Lancaster News 24 Mar 1906); the Hooper's Creek trestle wreck of a train carrying baseball fans in 1913 (30 Jul per the Yorkville Enquirer 1 Aug 1913, 30 Jun per wvncrails - date conflict, either way 1913); and service CONTINUED after the wreck - the night train's 'passenger coach' derailed and a new schedule 'Effective Sunday, December 27, 1914' for Trains 14, 15, 16 (Lancaster News 22 Dec 1914). Mixed trains ran on weekdays at some point before 1913, passenger-only on Sundays (wvncrails timetable caption) - mixed trains count (Rule 1). End 1916, exact: service across the river stopped 'the fifteenth day of July, 1916, when the steel bridge spanning the Catawba ... was taken away' (Lancaster News 24 Dec 1918; the OCR reads '1910', fixed as 1916 by the 'twenty-nine months' and the ICC's July 1916 washout). 3 ft gauge to 1902 (ICC; Trains magazine says 1906), then standard; steam. Headway is derived from the 1898 two-round-trip schedule (roughly every 8 h) and is an estimate for the other years.

segments.note: [OPEN] Through service resumed over the new Catawba bridge on 23 Dec 1918: 'For the first time in twenty-nine months ... the Lancaster and Chester Railway company ran a through passenger and freight train yesterday morning ... several cars of freight and one passenger coach ... several passengers made the initial trip', one train each way daily (Lancaster News 24 Dec 1918). Double daily service (Nos. 14-17) restored Wednesday 22 May 1919, 'practically the same service as was in effect before the floods of 1916' (Lancaster News 13 May 1919). Passenger service confirmed to 1919. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - service demonstrably ran past May 1919 by an unknown amount, and no source dates when it stopped; the Feb 1952 Official Guide (Dec 1951 entry) shows freight and express only, so it ended somewhere between mid-1919 and Dec 1951. The often-repeated claim that passenger service ended with the 1913 Hooper's Creek wreck is contradicted by the 1914, 1918 and 1919 reports. Do not extend without evidence. No 1917 segment: the line was cut by the flood from Jul 1916 to Dec 1918, and whether trains ran Chester - Fort Lawn in the gap is not established. USRA federal control (1917/18-1920) is not an ownership split. Steam (diesel from 1946-47). Headway is an estimate (one train each way, then two from May 1919).
